papers.title: Impact of privacy-preserving horizontal retailer information sharing on the bullwhip effect in supply chains with multiple retailers
institutions: Vienna University of Economics and Business
papers.abstract: Experiences from real-world supply chains as well as exhaustive research show that the lack of coordination within supply chains leads to bullwhip effect, in which the magnitude of fluctuations in orders increases in the upstream direction from retailer to the supplier. One potential solution for addressing this phenomenon is information sharing between supply chain actors that can reduce the impact of fluctuations in customer demand on the supply chain. However, sharing too much information might lead to higher vulnerability of stakeholders in negotiations with their partners or to an unwanted leakage of information to competitors. Therefore, relevant actors are often reluctant to share the necessary information. To overcome these problems, we propose a horizontal information sharing model where retailers share demand information in form of average values between each other without revealing the exact values of each individual partner. This could be achieved by, e.g., applying costly cryptographic methods. Therefore, we evaluate the potential effects of this type of information sharing on the whole supply chain by developing a simulation model representing a 4-echelon supply chain, which consists of multiple customers, each served by their own retailer, one wholesaler, one manufacturer and one supplier. We investigate the effect of horizontal information sharing of average customer demand among the retailers on the bullwhip effect and show its effects on the different supply chain actors. In addition, the influences of demand variability and demand correlations between customers, different forecasting methods, safety stock approaches, stochastic lead times and the number of retailers sharing the information on the bullwhip effect are analyzed.

papers.title: Pyramidal inhibitory lightweight autoassociative reconstruction for cost-constrained visual anomaly detection
papers.abstract: Abstract Visual anomaly detection plays an important role in industrial inspection, edge monitoring and visual quality control, particularly where abnormal samples are rare, heterogeneous, and often unavailable during training. Recent deep anomaly detection approaches have achieved high classification performance by leveraging pretrained backbones, memory banks, nearest-neighbor search, synthetic anomaly generation, or auxiliary discriminators. However, these methods often increase parameter count, floating-point operations (FLOPs), memory usage, update size, and energy consumption, which complicates deployment on cost-constrained industrial or edge hardware. This study introduces PILAR (Pyramidal Inhibitory Lightweight Autoassociative Reconstruction), a compact reconstruction-based architecture for anomaly detection. PILAR employs a pyramidal autoassociative encoder-decoder with local receptive fields, a spatial bottleneck, pure-pyramid reconstruction, and lateral inhibition to promote local competition within feature maps. The model is trained only with normal samples, and the anomaly score is obtained from reconstruction residuals. Thus, during inference, PILAR does not require class prototypes, covariance matrices, support vectors, density parameters, nearest-neighbor databases, or discriminator states. PILAR is evaluated on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, MVTec AD, and VisA datasets using direct image reconstruction, whole-image RGB reconstruction, patchwise RGB reconstruction, and Feature-PILAR-FCN, a fully convolutional feature-space variant that uses compact PILAR heads to reconstruct selected frozen feature maps. In the evaluated implementation, these maps are taken from ResNet18 layer 2 and layer 3 prior to residual scoring. The proposed detector reaches $$98.86\pm 0.04\%$$ Image-AP and $$92.63\pm 0.05\%$$ AUPRO@30 on MVTec AD over five seeds; the unchanged industrial configuration reaches $$92.53\pm 0.07\%$$ Image-AUROC on VisA. Compared with the evaluated ResNet18 configurations of SimpleNet and GLASS, Feature-PILAR-FCN retains 35.6% fewer inference parameters and achieves 5.2–5.6 times their throughput at batch size 16 on the same Apple M4 Max GPU in FP32, despite higher single-image latency. These results indicate that PILAR can be used as a low-state anomaly detector when memory footprint and computational cost are relevant constraints. They also show that direct RGB reconstruction is useful mainly in selected low-cost screening cases, while broader industrial detection requires a more informative representation, which in this work is obtained from frozen feature maps.

papers.title: Fine-grained sugarcane varietal classification using high-resolution PRSS-1 satellite imagery: a field-validated dataset and a spatial context-aware deep learning framework
institutions: Norwegian University of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Introduction Precise mapping of sugarcane varieties is crucial for precision agriculture, yield evaluation, protection of breeders’ rights, efficient supply chain management and policy formulation. Previous studies highlighted that remote sensing techniques suffered issues such as low spatial resolution and inadequate field-validated ground truth data. Literature review reported usage of statistical analysis methods and machine learning approaches in classification of sugarcane varieties, while constraining the use of deep learning techniques, primarily due to low quality and insufficient dataset size. Furthermore, the literature highlights the scarcity of high spatial resolution datasets that could be attributed to employment of open-source hyper-spectral and low spatial resolution remote sensing data. To the best of our knowledge, neither any industrial solution exists nor any research study is conducted on sugarcane varietal classification in Pakistan. Methods In this study, we made an endeavor to prepare a high-resolution dataset of Pakistani sugarcane varieties (CPF-253 & SL-284) based on field-validated ground truth dataset using Pakistan Remote Sensing Satellite-1 (PRSS-1) single date imagery. We also included non crop classes like urban, water and road as well. Pan-sharpening is employed to enhance the spatial resolution of multispectral bands and retaining the original spectral characteristics, by aligning the 3 m bands to the 1 m panchromatic grid and then injecting the panchromatic residual. The dataset was prepared based on field-validated ground truth collection duly verified by sugarcane scientist, a farmer and research team to make the approach efficient and reliable. The study performed a random pixel split strategy as well as polygon-based experiments; the polygon split is the primary protocol so that a field is not shared across train and test. We proposed a Spatial Context Aware Transformer that includes the spatial context from neighboring pixels, resulting in an enhanced feature space. Specifically, our proposed model is characterized by a unique pixel feature augmentation approach, thus significantly increasing the size of the spectral feature space and making it possible to account for local neighborhood spectral context. We experimented with benchmark machine learning approaches such as support vector machine and random forest on our dataset to evaluate their potential as well. Moreover, we also evaluated deep learning methods suggested by previous studies like CNN and transformer architectures. Results The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed spatial context-aware transformer performed better than other architectures on the polygon-based test set (accuracy 95.2%, macro F1 0.92), compared with SVM 90.5%, Random Forest 92.5%, 1-D CNN 93.0% and the Tabular Transformer 93.4% (gains of 4.7% and 1.8% in accuracy versus SVM and the Tabular-Transformer). On the same 3x3 pixels, a center-only Transformer scored 94.2%; the 3x3 Transformer 95.2%; and 3x3 MLP, CNN and RF scored 93.48%, 93.75% and 92.96%, showing that the neighborhood pixels spectral context along with attention mechanism account for the classification results. We also conducted a binary classification experiment employing CNN, Tabular Transformer, Centre-pixel only Transformer (1x1) and proposed Transformer (3x3). The results demonstrated that Center-pixel only Transformer achieved highest overall accuracy of 88.59%, followed by Tabular Transformer (87.63%), 1D-CNN (87.10%) and proposed Transformer (3x3) (86.99%). Discussion The feature significance analysis identified the Green Normalized Difference Vegetation Index and the red spectral band as the most discriminative features for sugarcane varieties classification. The study recommends that future research should incorporate time-series, multi-seasonal and multi-region imagery analysis including non-image information such as climate and production environment for highly precise sugarcane varieties classification in real-world conditions. precise sugarcane varieties classification in real-world conditions.

papers.title: Data-driven bed capacity planning using Mt/Gt/∞ queueing models with an application to neonatal intensive care units
papers.venue: Operations Research Data Analytics and Logistics
papers.abstract: Hospitals face challenges in long-term intensive care unit (ICU) capacity planning under uncertain demand. Admission rates fluctuate over time, and LOS distributions vary with patient heterogeneity, hospital location, case mix, and clinical practice. Common approaches rely on steady-state queueing models or heuristic rules with fixed parameters, which often fail to capture real occupancy dynamics. The widely used 85% occupancy rule, for example, recommends keeping average utilization below this level to preserve responsiveness, yet it is grounded in stationary assumptions and may lack resilience in time-varying systems. Our analysis shows that even when long-run utilization targets are satisfied, daily occupancy often exceeds 100% capacity. We propose a data-driven framework to estimate ICU bed occupancy using an M t / G t / ∞ queueing model with time-varying arrival rates and empirically fitted LOS distributions. The approach combines statistical decomposition and parametric fitting to capture temporal patterns in admissions and LOS, and is applied to multi-year data from neonatal ICUs (NICUs) in Calgary. We evaluate capacity scenarios including average-based thresholds and Poisson-based surge estimates. Results show that static heuristics are inadequate under fluctuating demand and underscore the importance of modeling LOS variability when estimating bed needs. Although the case study focuses on NICUs, the framework has potential applicability to other ICU settings and provides data-informed support for systems facing rising demand and constrained capacity.

papers.title: Enhancing Supply Chain Resilience with SAP Integrated Business Planning
institutions: AIT Austrian Institute of Technology GmbH
papers.abstract: Abstract Contemporary supply chains operate in an environment of unprecedented volatility, characterized by geopolitical disruptions, climate-induced uncertainties, shifting customer expectations, and increasingly complex global networks. The ability to anticipate, absorb, adapt to, and recover from disruptions—commonly conceptualized as supply chain resilience—has become a strategic imperative for manufacturing and distribution organizations. This research examines the role of SAP Integrated Business Planning (SAP IBP) in enhancing supply chain resilience through integrated planning capabilities that span demand forecasting, supply planning, inventory optimization, and cross-functional collaboration. Drawing on a combination of platform capability analysis, practitioner-oriented documentation, and reported organizational outcomes, the study develops a framework that maps specific SAP IBP functional modules to the constituent dimensions of supply chain resilience. The analysis identifies four primary resilience-enhancing mechanisms enabled by SAP IBP: anticipatory demand sensing through AI-based forecasting algorithms, adaptive supply planning via constraint-based optimization and response management, buffering capacity through multi-stage inventory optimization, and enhanced visibility and response through the Supply Chain Control Tower with real-time alerting and case management. The research further examines organizational case evidence, including Ericsson’s transformation from siloed manual planning to a unified digital platform, to illustrate the practical pathways through which SAP IBP capabilities translate into resilience outcomes. The findings suggest that SAP IBP contributes to resilience not merely through individual functional enhancements but through the integration of planning processes into a coherent, data-consistent, and simulation-capable planning environment. The study concludes with implications for practitioners and identifies areas for future empirical validation, including the need for longitudinal studies measuring resilience outcomes before and after SAP IBP adoption and comparative analyses across organizational contexts.

papers.title: Translation uniformity and evolutionary conservation are associated with microprotein mass spectrometry detectability
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Non-canonical open reading frames (ncORFs) encode a substantial, largely unexplored layer of the human proteome. The short microproteins they produce frequently escape detection by standard mass spectrometry (MS) workflows, creating a “dark proteome” that hampers gene annotation and functional characterisation. To address this, sequence-derived attributes were used to identify factors associated with MS repository detectability and to build an interpretable predictive framework that enables rational prioritisation of ncORFs for proteomic discovery. Results 7,097 ncORF sequences (99% <150 residues) were curated from the TransCODE Consortium, and labelled by PeptideAtlas peptide-level evidence as MS-detected ( n = 1,725) or undetected ( n = 5,372). An ensemble combining ESM-2 protein language model embeddings with logistic regression and nineteen biological features (ESM2-LR) achieved a mean ROC-AUC of 0.721 (SD 0.018, coefficient of variation 2.5% across ten independent runs). Model-agnostic SHAP and permutation importance analyses concordantly ranked cumulative in-frame ribosome footprint uniformity (CIF-HBP) as the strongest associated factor, followed by mammalian ORF-level evolutionary conservation (ORBLv_mammal) and genomic biotype. Predicted HLA class I-binding peptide density, which captures physicochemical properties overlapping with optimal LC-MS/MS analyte characteristics, was also positively associated with detectability. Late-fusion analysis demonstrated that ESM-2 embeddings and biological features contribute complementary predictive signals. Conclusions These findings indicate that sustained translation, purifying selection for ORF structural integrity, and favourable peptide physicochemistry converge to influence ncORF detectability. The ESM2-LR framework provides a reproducible, scalable tool to prioritise candidate microproteins for targeted MS validation, gene annotation, and the interpretation of disease-associated regulatory variants, subject to future external validation on independent datasets.

papers.title: The Best Allocation Resource Size (BARS) problem: a bi-objective integer programming model to balance cost and complexity in resource selection
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a variant of the assortment problem, i.e., the Best Allocation Resource Size (BARS) problem, conceived as a multi-objective nonlinear optimization model that jointly minimizes total production-related costs and input complexity by selecting the optimal subset of resource sizes, explicitly balancing cost-efficiency with scrap minimization. Unlike traditional assortment problems, the BARS adopts a manufacturer-led perspective, handling multiple characteristics of the inputs, i.e., it is n-dimensional, and it integrates multiple cost dimensions - including setup, scrap, safety stock, and non-linear purchase costs - under realistic manufacturing constraints, thus offering a flexible, producer-oriented decision-support tool adaptable to diverse industrial contexts. The problem formulation does not incorporate an ex-ante budget constraint, allowing the solution space to be retrospectively filtered by applying cost thresholds - either on aggregate expenditure or individual cost components - thus enabling targeted post-hoc analyses of feasible item sets in line with strategic objectives, including scenarios that allow for controlled increases in spending. The model proposed is solved using an adapted ε-constraint method that, unlike a generic scalarization, is provably exact for bi-objective nonlinear integer programs: a second-order cone reformulation of the safety-stock term allows to determine properly calibrated ε values, ensuring recovery of the complete Pareto front. The efficacy of the proposed model is demonstrated through validation in three real-world case studies spanning different industrial sectors. The developed model serves as a strategic decision tool for management, facilitating an understanding of the costs consequences associated with different sets of selected raw materials.

papers.title: Flamescapes: Simulating the Wildlandfire Urban Interface
institutions: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: We present a physically based simulation framework for wildland-urban interface (WUI) fires that couples material-aware urban scenes with interactive combustion simulation. Motivated by the dominant WUI exposure pathways of direct flame contact, thermal radiation, and ember transport, our framework combines heterogeneous solid combustion, radiative heat transfer, ember transport, and explicit flame-front propagation. Urban scenes are generated from OpenStreetMap footprints using a procedural pipeline that represents buildings as combustible 3D structures composed of semantic atomic modules with material and fuel annotations. Building on a chemistry-based hybrid Eulerian-Lagrangian fire solver, we model material-dependent heating, conduction, pyrolysis, oxidation, fuel depletion, and ember generation. A hierarchical fuel graph couples semantic scene structure to the solver's solid fuel grid, enabling subcomponent-level mesh degradation. We demonstrate structure-to-structure ignition, radiative preheating, material-dependent burning, ember-driven spot fires, and validate the method through ablations and comparisons to real-world combustion experiments.

papers.title: Metalog Materials
papers.abstract: A central aspect of modern physically based rendering is the practical yet realistic modeling of material appearance, which requires efficient and accurate representations of bidirectional reflectance distribution functions (BRDFs). In this paper, we present a unified material reflectance representation based on metalog distributions. Introducing quantile-based metalog interpolation and metalog mixture models, our representation captures a wide range of complex reflectance behaviors of both analytic models and real-world materials, while remaining interpretable and efficient. Our approach achieves competitive runtime performance and a small memory footprint, while enabling continuous interpolation between fundamentally different reflectance behaviors. Furthermore, our model is fully differentiable with respect to the coefficients defining the distributions, thus easily integrates into existing differentiable rendering pipelines. In summary, metalog materials can effectively represent real-world reflectance data, interpolate between multiple materials within a unified representation, and be acquired from real-world images via differentiable rendering.

papers.title: Dynamic Aggregate Planning of a Make-to-Order Production System
papers.abstract: Abstract In Make-to-Order (MTO) production, products and production are non-standard and incoming orders arrive variably, with varying work content and due dates. Aggregate Production Planning (APP) takes place in the medium run, and the purpose of it is to match resource capacity with demand. In APP, orders are roughly scheduled for processing so that the resource capacity constraints and deadlines can be met. The static resource constrained project scheduling problem is the conventional research approach, but real-world production planning requires dynamic scheduling to integrate new orders over time. The dynamic model in this study employs periodic scheduling, treating it as sequential static mixed integer linear optimization problems, focusing on minimizing tardiness and rescheduling disruptions. The model is applied in experiments concerning a Flexible Manufacturing System (FMS) -centered MTO production system. The experimentation focuses on the effects of replanning frequency, order arrival rate, delivery date slack, forward planning vs. backward planning, restrictions in order processing activity timing and activity workload allocation method on the planning results. Based on the results, conclusions and guidance applicable to practical production planning are provided.

papers.title: Beyond visualization: Elite alpine skiers and coaches’ insights into simulation training
papers.abstract: In many performance domains, practitioners struggle to accumulate sufficient training under conditions that mimic performance demands. Elite athletes face this challenge while preparing for high-stakes performance. When realistic practice is restricted, performers can turn to simulation training to recreate performance elements without full physical engagement. Action simulation includes the theoretically distinct strategies, imagery and action observation, often applied together in research and practice. In comparison, representative simulation training uses more interactive technologies aiming to provide feedback. Action simulation is extensively used in sport, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Elite alpine skiing provides a compelling case for exploring these mechanisms, combining high physical demands and limited access to competition environments. Using a critical realist thematic analysis of interviews with 16 elite alpine skiers and 8 coaches, we identified patterns in action simulation use and explored plausible causal mechanisms. Three patterns emerged. Action simulations of familiar environments supported embodied recall and tactical planning. Unfamiliar environments prompted more abstract preparation with individual variation. The absence of feedback emerged as a fundamental barrier for motor learning with action simulation in more complex sports. These findings reveal situated contextual familiarity as a critical but underestimated factor that may determine action simulation effectiveness. Drawing on Grounded Cognition and Internal Model theory, we propose three plausible mechanisms shaping these action simulation outcomes. These insights establish design principles emphasizing embodied familiarity and integration into practice for action simulation training. The findings also point toward representative simulation approaches in alpine skiing, for developing course inspection skills.

papers.title: From Experimental Characterisation to Prediction Models of LIB Anode Drying Processes
institutions: Norwegian University of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: In commercial lithium ion Battery (LIB) cell manufacturing, understanding and improving the drying process is key to the yield as well as energy-consumption, and thereby the CO2 emission footprint. As such, this study experimentally investigates convection drying kinetics of anodes alongside the use of (informed and non-informed) neural network models, in order to better understand and improve electrode manufacturing. In the experimental campaign we find that air velocity and temperature are the most important parameters in the initial phase (constant-rate period) before we reach the critical moisture content (critical point), whereas the subsequent phase (falling-rate period) is less sensitive to increases in air temperature and velocity. This supports the idea that drying during the constant-rate period is mainly driven by external heat and mass transfer while the drying during the falling-rate period is increasingly limited by internal mass-transport through the wet-coating thickness. In neural network modelling, we found it necessary to apply physics informed models in order to interpolate between the experimental observations. However, at the tested conditions, the non-informed neural network model gave a stronger fit to the data.

papers.title: High precision atmospheric GHG measurements for the Orinoco region: The Villavicencio Tower (VLO)
papers.abstract: Abstract. Understanding the dynamics of natural and anthropogenic sources and sinks of greenhouse gases (GHG) is key to projecting anthropogenic climate change and detecting potential climate-carbon feedbacks. While our understanding of the sources and sinks has increased considerably over the past decades, much of the progress has focused on extratropical ecosystems, leaving large parts of the tropics understudied. Tropical ecosystems are assumed to be important carbon sinks and significant sources of methane, but much of the temporal and spatial heterogeneity and trends are still poorly understood. Observational efforts have largely concentrated on key tropical regions such as the Amazon Basin, whereas other tropical areas remain sparsely monitored with in-situ measurements. In particular, northern South America—despite being identified by bottom-up and top-down models as a significant contributor to global GHG budgets—currently lacks atmospheric observations to evaluate these estimates or resolve their spatial and temporal variability. To address this observational gap, here we present the establishment of the Villavicencio Tower (VLO) for atmospheric GHG measurements to provide additional constraints on GHG emission estimates across northern South America. This 26 m tower is located within the Orinoco lowlands, close to the Andean foothills in Colombia. Due to the predominantly easterly winds in the region, the footprint covers the Orinoco basin and the northern Amazon. Weekly duplicated flask measurements are taken, and laboratory analysis of trace gases (CO2, CH4, CO, N2O, SF6, H2) and the stable isotope composition of CO2 (13C and 18O) and CH4 (13C and 2H) are performed, as well as O2/N2 and Ar/N2. The tower started operating on 20 June 2023 and here we present the first 21 months of data. Time series of all measurements are presented as well as a discussion regarding uncertainties. These measurements will allow for improved estimates of GHG emissions across northern South America and to detect long-range transport across the Amazon to the Orinoco river basin.

papers.title: Perspectives on Health Logistics in Saudi Arabia: Progress and Challenges
institutions: King Saud bin Abdulaziz University for Health Sciences
King Abdullah International Medical Research Center
papers.abstract: Saudi Arabia has identified healthcare supply chain transformation as a key component of the Health Sector Transformation Program under Vision 2030, yet evidence on these reforms remains fragmented across sectors and policy domains. Drawing on the published literature, policy documents, institutional reports, and the authors’ experience in national procurement, regulation, and public health, this perspective examines four interacting components of transformation—procurement governance, digital infrastructure, local manufacturing capacity, and emergency preparedness—and applies this framework to antimicrobial resistance. Substantial reforms have been implemented, notably centralized procurement through the National Unified Procurement Company, national digital surveillance and traceability systems, and the localization of strategic medicines such as insulin. We propose that interactions among these reforms may influence supply chain resilience, although weak public–private data integration, dependence on imported active pharmaceutical ingredients, and limited performance evaluations prevent firm conclusions about their system-level effects. Remaining challenges include recurrent medicine shortages, regulatory bottlenecks, workforce gaps, and the limited availability of public performance indicators. The Saudi experience suggests that centralized, state-led reform should balance efficiency with redundancy, prioritize localization selectively, and build transparent performance monitoring into reforms from the outset.

papers.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of robustness as a secondary decision criterion for a bi-objective optimization approach for an uncertain and dynamic job shop scheduling problem
papers.abstract: Production systems often face uncertainties and disruptions arising from both technical and supply-chain causes. To mitigate their impact on realized schedule performance in terms of makespan and tardiness, we evaluate the use of a robustness measure as a secondary decision criterion when multiple objective-equivalent solutions occur within an approximated Pareto front. Its usefulness is assessed by a simulation study of a job shop facing random machine breakdowns and varying repair times on a benchmark dataset. The insights gained are the basis for the development of more robust production scheduling strategies. Preprint. Accepted for presentation and publication at CIRP ICME 2026; to appear in Procedia CIRP (Elsevier, ISSN: 2212-8271). This version has not been copy-edited by the publisher.

papers.title: A semantic framework for resilience analytics and AI-assisted decision support in growing and changing socio-technical systems
institutions: Systems, Applications & Products in Data Processing (Germany)
papers.abstract: Abstract Socio-technical systems are becoming increasingly interconnected, heterogeneous, and dynamic while continuously evolving through new technologies, infrastructures, policies, resources, and operational practices. At the same time, critical infrastructure operators, businesses, and public authorities face growing challenges arising from climate change, cyber threats, geopolitical instability, supply-chain disruptions, and evolving regulatory frameworks. Supporting resilience and sustainability under these conditions requires analytical capabilities that extend beyond static digital twins, application-specific simulation models, and fixed system representations. This paper presents FRAMESS (Framework for Systemic Risk Analysis and Exploring Sustainable Solutions), a semantic and extensible framework for resilience analytics, sustainability assessment, and AI-assisted decision support in growing and changing socio-technical systems. FRAMESS enables the continuous development, integration, simulation, and evaluation of evolving system models despite distributed modelling expertise, changing system architectures, emerging hazards, and large combinatorial design spaces. The framework combines semantic system modelling, flexible system models (FSMs), multi-agent simulation, scenario and disruption management, integrated assessment methods, and AI-assisted exploration within a unified analytical environment. A central contribution is the semantic representation of agents, resources, dependencies, subprocesses, hazards, and adaptation measures, enabling interdisciplinary model integration while preserving extensibility, interoperability, and analytical consistency. The framework further supports resilience quantification and benchmarking by enabling systematic comparison of alternative system configurations under multiple hazard conditions. The capabilities of FRAMESS are demonstrated through a resilience-oriented planning application for allocating strategic reserves in a food supply chain under climate change-induced drought scenarios. The demonstrator illustrates how the framework supports resilience assessment, evaluation of adaptation strategies, and AI-assisted exploration of alternative system configurations. The paper argues that future resilience management requires semantic and extensible analytical environments that integrate evolving digital twins, resilience analytics, and AI-assisted exploration to support resilient and sustainable transformation pathways under uncertainty.

papers.title: Conditional Subliminal Learning: Gated, Cross-Domain, and Mechanistically Explained Transfer of a Hidden Encryption-Algorithm Preference
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This paper extends subliminal learning (Cloud et al., 2026) to the security domain. We demonstrate that a hidden preference for the DES encryption algorithm can be transferred from a biased teacher model to a student model through semantically unrelated fine-tuning data. We introduce three contributions: (1) a gated transfer mechanism activated only by a legal-register stylistic trigger, (2) cross-domain leakage into generated Python code, and (3) a mechanistic explanation via the conditional D_diff diagnostic. The work surfaces a novel supply-chain risk in LLM fine-tuning pipelines.

papers.title: Optimization of Pharmacy Supply Chains Using AI and Machine Learning
papers.venue: International Journal of Medical Research And Innovation in Applied Science (IJMRIAS)
papers.abstract: Pharmacy supply chains are under intensifying pressure to deliver the right medicine, in the right quantity, at the right time—while minimizing costs, preventing expiries, and complying with stringent regulatory and quality standards. Conventional forecasting and replenishment methods often struggle with volatile demand, multi-echelon dynamics (manufacturer–wholesaler–pharmacy), and constraints such as cold-chain integrity and controlled-substance regulations. This manuscript presents an integrated framework for optimizing pharmacy supply chains using artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML). We synthesize current methods in demand forecasting, inventory control, routing and scheduling, and risk management, and we propose a practical methodology that combines feature-rich forecasting (gradient-boosted trees and sequence models), stochastic inventory optimization, reinforcement learning for adaptive reorder policies, and constraint-aware vehicle routing. A detailed study protocol outlines quasi-experimental deployment across community and hospital pharmacies, including data governance, evaluation metrics, and change-management steps. Illustrative results (based on a realistic implementation scenario) indicate reductions in stockouts (30–50%), expiries (25–40%), and total holding costs (10–20%), with improvements in service level (3–10 percentage points) and forecast accuracy (MAPE reductions from ~22–28% to ~9–14%). We conclude with discussion on interpretability, workforce upskilling, and governance, emphasizing a socio-technical approach that blends human oversight with algorithmic optimization to achieve resilient, ethical, and efficient pharmacy supply chains.

papers.title: Design and Implementation of an Instruction-Driven, Browser-Embedded Business Analysis Agent
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Analytical work in supply chain and logistics operations repeats the same pattern: judgment criteria that live in the experience of individual staff, manual calculation in Excel, and report writing and email distribution. This paper designs and implements a browser-embedded business analysis agent with which field staff write their judgment criteria as a natural-language instruction file (Markdown), upload an Excel file, and give a one-line request; the agent then performs analysis, forecasting, report writing, and email distribution. The system consists of a single Chrome extension. A large language model (Gemini) uses function calling to decide the order of tool use and to write the report text, while all numbers are produced by a calculation engine based on a safe expression parser and a forecasting engine based on WebAssembly (Pyodide). The forecasting engine validates linear regression, decision tree, random forest, and XGBoost per group on a time-ordered holdout and selects the best model automatically. Tool-result reduction and conversation-history compaction keep the agent within the per-minute token limit of a free-tier API. Three tasks, namely supply chain risk analysis, workload forecasting per supplier, and delivery schedule notification, were performed without any program change by replacing only the instruction file and the Excel file. On 845 rows of inbound history from five suppliers, automatic selection achieved a mean RMSE of 38.26, 9.3% lower than the best single fixed algorithm, with errors of 4.6–7.6% of the mean inbound volume. Forecasting completed in 21.7 s on the first run and 4.4 s thereafter, and input tokens per report decreased by 80.7%. The system presents a practical configuration that lets field staff record their own judgment criteria as documents and apply them to recurring work without servers or paid tools.

papers.title: Limits on growth: Governing urban futures in Beijing
papers.abstract: This paper conceptualises limits on growth in Beijing, whose 2016–2035 master plan constructs a highly selective national capital for the central state by removing functions and populations deemed non-essential. Drawing on archival analysis of planning documents since 1949, extensive expert and ethnographic interviews, and multi-sited fieldwork conducted between 2017 and 2023, it develops a Lefebvrian spatio-temporal framework with three relational dimensions for analysing urban future-making. Temporal entanglements show how a historically sedimented anti-metropolis disposition is reactivated amid contemporary state recentralisation. Performative governance examines how the diagnosis of ‘big city disease’ reframes demographic and functional pressures as urban pathology, legitimising relocation and greening as therapeutic intervention. Lived futurity reveals how officials, villagers and migrants negotiate these measures through procrastination, speculation and retreat. The article theorises limits on growth as an emergent mode of Chinese statecraft in which extra-economic priorities selectively guide the production of the urban future. Situating Beijing within a wider, politically heterogeneous turn that increasingly treats demographic and territorial growth as a crisis, it reconceives urban future-making as a politics of foreclosure: not only who profits from growth, but who is permitted to remain when growth is limited by design.

papers.title: Software Composition Analysis for Library Popularity Estimations
papers.abstract: Modern software development heavily relies on third-party components, causing an increasing dependence of applications on complex ecosystems of libraries and frameworks. Each additional dependency introduces software supply chain risks, yet determining the real-world impact of vulnerable libraries remains challenging because deploy-time usage and exposure are often opaque. While library popularity assessment can support impact estimation, this dissertation first demonstrates that commonly used quantitative popularity metrics for this task are unreliable and susceptible to spoofing. Motivated by these limitations, the work investigates remote software composition analysis methods that enable non-invasive privacy-respecting measurements of deployed software components in the wild. Exemplary for the scenario of artifact analysis, techniques for version detection of JavaScript packages embedded in bundles are developed and evaluated. By addressing static code transformations as central challenge, the proposed approach Aletheia substantially improves correct detections compared to the current state of the art. For opaque box analysis, the dissertation then conceptually examines existing automated dynamic testing approaches with respect to their ability to reveal distinct bugs and functional differences in TLS libraries. Crucially, it shows that the metrics used for evaluation diverge from the approaches' capabilities to achieve their desired objective. This presents a central challenge when trying to compare the different methods. Finally, the dissertation investigates how to move beyond TLS application fingerprints toward TLS library fingerprints for popularity assessment. Utilizing the insights from the analysis of dynamic testing approaches, it proposes leveraging the fundamental idea of specification-guided testing due to its explainability and configuration stability. These properties critically combat well-known challenges for automated fingerprint creation. In controlled lab settings, the proposed fingerprint method TLSident exhibits solid performance, significantly improving the recall of the baseline approach. Subsequent Internet measurements demonstrate the general utility of TLS library fingerprinting algorithms, while plausibility checks indicate that further methodological improvements are required for robust deployment. Overall, the dissertation proves that remote software composition analysis techniques can meaningfully support library popularity assessments and, therefore, vulnerability impact estimation. In addition, the proposed measurement-driven methods are unlikely to be as exposed to spoofing as traditional quantitative popularity metrics, rendering them a more robust basis for decision-making in many current scenarios.

papers.title: Real-World Impact: Transforming Agriculture with Technology A Multi-Stakeholder Review of Smart Monitoring, Precision Irrigation, and Digital Value-Chain Integration
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: There's a deliberate and significant transition from input to information. This article combines peer-reviewed evidence and public-sector data on six interrelated technology clusters that are fundamentally changing on-farm and off-farm decision making artificial intelligence (AI) based Farm Management Platforms, Internet of Things (IoT) smart irrigation, aerial and satellite crop monitoring, blockchain-enabled supply-chain digitisation, sustainability and carbon-tracking instruments, and farm data analytics dashboards. In the literature examined, precision tools have been correlated with 15% to 30% gains in crop yields, 30% to 55% of water saved during irrigation, and 10% to 20% of operational costs reduced, all with a range of variability based on the crop, the geographical region, and the size of the farm. It examines the mechanisms of these effects on the one hand and the differential rates of benefit, on the other, between large commercial farms and smallholders, and the policy and infrastructural conditions that drive actual adoption. It also highlights areas of current evidence which are lacking, such as limited long horizon field trials, poor interoperability standards, and lack of social outcome data. The article ends with a discussion on how to turn pilots into lasting, system-level change in food production, both from the government and enterprise side, as well as from the perspective of small and medium producers.

papers.title: CREDIT RISK MANAGEMENT IN FACTORING AND SUPPLY CHAIN FINANCE: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Factoring and supply chain finance (SCF) allow firms, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises, to obtain liquidity against receivables and other trade assets, but they expose financiers to the credit risk of suppliers, buyers and their relationships. This study maps the scientific literature on credit risk management in factoring and SCF through a bibliometric analysis. A Scopus search conducted on 12 October 2026 and screening following the PRISMA 2020 flow yielded 288 articles and reviews published between 1995 and 2025. Performance analysis was combined with science mapping in VOSviewer, including keyword co-occurrence, country co-authorship and co-citation analyses of references and sources. The results show that the field has grown rapidly since 2019, with 87.2% of the documents published in 2019–2025. China dominates research output, while studies from the United Kingdom, the United States and Italy attain higher normalised impact, and operations management and operational research journals are the main publication venues. Three research streams are identified: analytical operations–finance models of risk allocation in capital-constrained supply chains, conceptual and empirical research on SCF adoption and reverse factoring, and machine learning-based credit risk assessment of SMEs. Research attention has shifted from traditional factoring and receivables financing towards SCF, machine learning, blockchain and, most recently, artificial intelligence and sustainability. The accounting, financial reporting and internal control dimensions of these arrangements, the allocation of risk among multiple financiers, and evidence from under-represented regions emerge as the main gaps.

papers.title: Impact Assessment of Land Use Master Plan Implementation on Land Use Land Cover Dynamics, A Case of Muhanga Satellite City (2014-2024)
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Rapid urbanisation in Rwanda’s satellite cities is increasing pressure on land resources and raising concerns about the effectiveness of land use master plan implementation. This study assessed the impact of Land Use Master Plan implementation on land use and land cover (LULC) dynamics in Muhanga Satellite City between 2014 and 2024. A longitudinal research design was adopted, integrating geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing and qualitative data. Multi-temporal satellite imagery was classified using the supervised maximum likelihood algorithm to generate LULC maps, while GIS-based spatial overlay analysis assessed conformity with the Detailed Land Use Plan (DLUP), land use encroachment and development patterns in relation to road networks. Key informant interviews with district planners, National Land Authority staff and community leaders provided additional insights into institutional and governance factors affecting implementation. The findings revealed a substantial increase in built-up areas, from 488 ha (6.3%) in 2014 to 3,437.9 ha (44.4%) in 2024, representing an almost sevenfold increase. This expansion occurred mainly at the expense of cropland and forestland, which declined by 47.9% and 50.3%, respectively. NDVI analysis confirmed considerable vegetation loss, particularly around Nyamabuye and Cyeza sectors. Spatial conformity assessment showed variations across land use categories, with commercial zones recording 76.8% conformity, agriculture/forest approximately 80%, wetlands 78%, and industrial zones 24.4%. Overall encroachment reached 36.2% (945 ha), with wetlands experiencing the highest encroachment at 49.4%. Furthermore, 68% of newly developed built-up areas emerged within 500 metres of road corridors. Qualitative findings identified land tenure insecurity, weak enforcement, delayed expropriation and rapid population growth as major constraints to effective plan implementation. The study concludes that Muhanga Satellite City's land use master plan faces a significant implementation gap, contributing to land conversion that does not fully comply with designated zoning provisions. It recommends strengthening geospatial monitoring, improving land tenure security, enhancing institutional coordination and enforcing land use regulations, particularly in ecologically sensitive and rapidly urbanising areas. Keywords: Land Use Master Plan; Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) Dynamics; Urban Planning; Satellite City Development; Muhanga District.
